title: Metagenomic sequencing with a neural network detects pathogens and cancer in lung biopsies
summary: Lung biopsies from 133 patients underwent Illumina and Nanopore metagenomic sequencing. Neural networks pretrained on human reads from 2,095 sequencing results predicted cancer risk; against histology the Illumina pipeline had 83.7% sensitivity and 97.6% specificity and diagnosed 36 additional cancer patients. Pathogen detection had 77.6% sensitivity and 97.6% specificity against a composite reference standard (Nanopore 34.7% and 98.7%); the study is single-centre and the neural network applies only to the cancer call.
